title: FP8 temporal activation smoothing and latency-aware fallback for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: During progressive FP8 enablement on Hopper we continue to see short-lived inference instability driven by transient per-layer activation outliers and bursty request tails. These manifest as occasional quality regressions and elevated p99 latency when the quantization scale estimate reacts too quickly to a noisy minibatch. Goal: introduce a low-risk runtime mitigation that smooths activation scale estimates over time, adds a short hysteresis window, and attaches a latency-aware automatic fallback to a compatible mode (INT8/FP16) when stability signals cross thresholds. The mechanism should be lightweight (no per-token blocking on the critical path), configurable per-model and per-shard, and observable for correlation with calibration/eval artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Golden-eval regression <= 0.5% MRR loss across representative benchmark for E4M3/E5M2 after 2 weeks on 10% canary. 2) Median latency change <= 2% and p99 within SLO (+/-100ms). 3) Runtime fallback rate <= 1% on canary traffic after stabilization period. 4) Dashboard surfaced: per-layer EMA scale, fallback counts, activation kurtosis, and overflow events. 5) Automated canary gating rules trigger rollback on quality or latency regressions. 6) Unit + integration tests that simulate bursty activations and assert deterministic fallback behavior.
implementation_notes: Design: (a) Per-layer EMA: maintain an exponential moving average of observed activation scale with configurable alpha (default 0.1) and min-window enforcement to avoid noisy immediate switches; store EMA per-shard so rollout can be staged. (b) Short-term smoothing buffer: keep last N scale samples (N=5) and compute median-trim to protect against single-sample spikes. (c) Hysteresis policy: require X consecutive samples beyond threshold or sustained latency > SLO for Y ms before flipping quant profile; Y defaults to 250ms. (d) Latency-aware fallback: if request-level p99 latency delta or variance metric exceeds configured threshold OR if kernel overflow counters spike, mark request for fallback to INT8/FP16; fallback is per-request, not global, and emits diagnostic header. (e) Calibration pipeline: expose smoothing params to offline calibrator and golden-set evaluator so calibration can compute expected stabilized scales. (f) Safe-mode: a global kill-switch and percent-based rollouts in runtime config. Implementation touches: runtime kernel (scale estimator), request router (fallback header), calibration service (emit stabilized profile), and telemetry hooks.
telemetry_requirements: Emit new metrics and logs: 1) per-layer scale_ema (histogram), 2) scale_sample_count, 3) activation_kurtosis / skew (histogram), 4) fallback_trigger_reason (tagged counts: latency, overflow, divergence), 5) per-request latency delta relative to baseline, 6) per-shard fallback_rate, 7) golden-set per-eval accuracy deltas by model+profile. Create Grafana dashboards and Alert rules: (A) fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 30m -> P1 alert, (B) golden-set MRR drop > 0.8% -> P0, (C) activation kurtosis spikes -> investigate calibration drift. Add traces to link request -> fallback decision -> kernel telemetry.
rollout_plan: 1) Dev-local: unit + kernel-level deterministic tests. 2) Shadow canary: enable smoothing and emit fallback decisions in shadow mode on internal traffic (1 week). 3) 1% external traffic canary for 48h with automated gating. 4) 10% canary for 7 days (monitor golden-set and latency). 5) 50% for 3 days. 6) Gradual ramp to 100% with performance monitoring and automatic rollback if any gate trips. Rollback criteria defined in acceptance_criteria. During each stage, run golden-seed eval nightly and snapshot key telemetry. Provide rollback runbook and playbook for manual override.
